pillar_reactions.evidence: Interrupted the pitch to endorse it and tie it to his own reasoning: 'Yeah, exactly that is the thing that I liked, and the reason why I'm here... the thing I saw in that video was like, it's not only, it's like the mixture of sport and workout... it's something that attacks both angles, not only muscle building, but also flexibility'. He then completed the rep's own longevity example about standing up unaided at 75.

Rep positioned it as already handled — 'nutrition for you is from what I'm hearing... already to in the gym... Trevor probably would mainly fine-tune it' — and gave the three-variable frame with an explicit adjustment for his difficulty gaining weight ('you can probably eat more and you don't have to keep this strict window'). No questions and no pushback.

Agreed in the moment ('I agree') and then, unprompted and at length, argued the case for it better than the rep had: 'I do a push-up, and I'm thinking, like, damn, I have no idea if I did this push-up the right way or not... if there was somebody standing right next to me telling me like hey no those legs aren't straight, I'd be correcting them, but I don't have it and I don't have the money to pay it so so be it.' He conceded the pillar completely and still did not buy — the value was accepted and the price was not.

anchors.raw: Everything, all the knowledge, everything, it's on YouTube. You can look it up. / Yeah, that's exactly my point. Right now, I'm doing it on YouTube.
anchors.note: The strongest anchor in the batch, and it is at zero. He is three weeks in, motivated, and it is working — 'I've done it very good. I'm very motivated.' The rep conceded the content point outright, which left only accountability to carry the whole $6,000 delta.

anchors.raw: I just bought the protein today and I thought like damn this is a good investment if I really want to do this and that was like 25 dollars
anchors.note: His reference for a meaningful fitness purchase is $25. The gap to $6,000 is 240x and he stated it himself: '6k is like five and a half k more than I could ever think of.'

anchors.raw: I pay my rent, but I need a house. And I pay Netflix, because I love movies. And I pay delicious food. I'm in Italy right now. And I'm eating amazingly. And I spend a lot of money on food. But that's a priority for me. My physique... Not that much.
anchors.note: He ranked his own spending honestly and put physique below food and streaming. The rep caught it correctly — 'So it turns out, it's not a priority for you' — but had no move to change the ranking, and the prospect stood by both his stated why and his ranking simultaneously.

anchors.raw: I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then write it a bit, and then see if I really like it, and then see if that's really a priority, and then buy another one that's 20, and then see, and after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.
anchors.note: He is anchored to a ladder, not a number. His objection is to buying the top rung first, given a personal history of quitting within two weeks — which is arguably a rational read of his own risk, and there is no lower rung to sell him.

anchors.raw: my current cash is zero... I have the exact cash I need to pay my credit cards that I which I've used to buy the tickets to fly to italy
anchors.note: A hard floor rather than a perception. Disclosed under the rep's own financial-picture questioning, and it is the point at which the money play should have ended rather than progressing to third-party finance.

unmet_demand.want: A cheaper entry rung — a small, low-commitment product to test whether he sticks with it before committing $6,000
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme sells only 6- and 12-month one-to-one coaching. Nothing exists between the free content that brought him in and a $6,000 ticket, and he articulated the missing rung precisely with the bicycle analogy.

unmet_demand.want: Form correction on the bodyweight calisthenics he is actually doing — 'I have no idea if I did this push-up the right way or not'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme does exactly this, by video review, but for kettlebell movements; the rep described the mechanism without ever connecting it to the specific need the prospect had just voiced. The capability is close to what he asked for and was never mapped onto it.

unmet_demand.want: A reason to believe that paying changes the outcome when the free version is already working
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep conceded that all the knowledge is free and rested the entire differential on accountability. The prospect agreed accountability is the differentiator and still declined, so the offer has no evidence — outcome data, retention figures, a comparison against self-directed training — to close that gap with.

unmet_demand.want: Payment spread over time at a size he could carry from monthly income
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep stated there are no set payment plans and jumped straight to a third-party financing partner, which the prospect rejected on principle at that ticket size rather than on terms. No instalment option owned by the company was ever put on the table.
